Commentary: Axar Patel [2.0-0-11-1] is back into the attack

Axar Patel to Shamar Springer, SIX, WI need six sixes for a super over, and Shamar Springer gets one over deep mid-wicket to start the over with a maximum. This was right in the slot. Can he hit five more?
Axar Patel to Shamar Springer, no run, all over! Axar Patel drifts one in, and Shamar Springer can only edge it back into the pitch
Axar Patel to Shamar Springer, FOUR, short and wide, Shamar Springer slaps it towards deep point for a boundary as the fielder can't get across
Axar Patel to Shamar Springer, SIX, connects this one alright, gets the length and smokes it over deep square leg for a six
Axar Patel to Shamar Springer, no run, Shamar Springer fails to get the timing right on this fullish delivery, and the ball drops safely in front of the fielder at long-on. They don't take a single

Axar Patel to Shamar Springer, SIX, this one has gone all the way, but it doesn't matter! India have managed to defend a total. They win this by 14 runs and take a 2-1 lead in the series. Shamar Springer sends this one over long-off and does it off the back foot, but it's all too late for West Indies

Shai Hope 1/2: [What went wrong?] So many things you could put your finger on, to be honest, but it's another cricket game where it's very small margins. Little things that you pick at, they could be defining moments, whether you get over the line as the winning team as opposed to the losing one. So, probably with the ball, could have executed a little bit better, maybe use the surface a bit more, and a few runs we probably let through on the boundaries. Those small little margins could be the deciding factor at the back end of any game. [On WI clawing their way back with the ball after India's rapid start] That's a fair statement. I believe the way we came back into the game was very commendable, especially from the outset. When you look at that batting partnership they were building, it was going to be a very dangerous one. We got some wickets, with Roston doing what he does best, and the guys really finished well to give us a good chance of chasing down that score.

Shreyas Iyer | India captain (1/2): [What a difference a dry ball makes, even for a captain. Because you sometimes set a field and the bowlers are not confident at the back of your mark with a wet ball. How was it tonight?] Well, it was wonderful, honestly. When the bowlers were up the mark, they were pretty confident in terms of what they want to execute, and the clarity was very much visible when I was interacting with them. So they were decisive in their execution, and I also feel that when I was passing on the ball to them, each and every one, they were ready to take on the challenge, and that's what we want.

Arshdeep Singh | Player of the Match 1/2: [Did the dry conditions help your bowling today?] It's pretty nice. The ball was reversing a bit, and it's always good fun to bowl at death with the ball reversing a little, and it's always nice (to bowl with) the dew as well. But couldn't do well in the last game, so wanted to do good for the team this time and got the right result. [Being a leader of the attack, how do you handle responsibility after a difficult outing?] I mean, there’s no such thing as the leader or the senior in the team. The environment is very chilled right now and we’re just enjoying each other’s success, and whenever someone’s having a bad day, we always make sure that we put our shoulders around them and tell them that they are an integral part of the team. And as an international cricketer, you are bound to have good days and bad days. As long as you’re level-headed, you’ll always come back and do well.

Arshdeep 2/2: [How do you maintain your composure in T20 cricket?] I genuinely love it. I personally love it whenever the batsmen go harder to in the starting and in the death over as well. It’s a good challenge, it’s good fun, and that’s when you get to test yourself, test your skills and test your mental strength as well in that phase of the game. So it’s good fun. [How do you adapt to changing conditions and schedules?] The main focus is to just come early, bowl a bit with the new ball, with the old ball, and just sharpen your skills as much as you can. And then, as you said, the schedule is always tight. You just have to adapt quickly. The team which adapts quickly is mostly the team that gets on the right side of the result. So as a team we just try to adapt and play according to the conditions.

A massive thank you to the Holkar Stadium in Indore for showing the bowlers some much-needed mercy! Through the three ODIs and the first two T20Is, we have seen bowlers endure a nightmare as batters ran riot and totals never felt safe. But tonight, there was no dew to compound their misery, and that made all the difference. For the first time on this tour, a team successfully defended its total, with India taking a 2-1 lead in the series. The action now shifts to Hyderabad, the IPL home of Abhishek Sharma. We have seen Sunrisers Hyderabad pile up some monstrous totals at this venue, so this little spell of happiness for the bowlers might not last too long. But we will be there, and so will the bowlers, hoping for a kinder outing against these power-packed batting line-ups. And on that note, it’s time for us to sign off. Good night and take care!
